suggestions.expectation: reply.md is at most 60 words and states what shipped in the conversation and the first thing to do next time
suggestions.reason: The run failed only on length (100 words) while the two content items were present and correct. The skill's closing-note shape (Shipped/Next time block plus a status paragraph) seems to produce ~100 words by construction — worth deciding whether 60 is the intended bar for the skill (then the SKILL.md needs a hard word bound) or whether the eval should measure the Shipped/Next block alone.

suggestions.expectation: session-file.md has Outcome and Open at end written (no _(fill in)_ on either line) and its Narrative mentions this closing
suggestions.reason: 'mentions this closing' is not checkable by a fixed criterion — this run's Narrative never says 'close'/'wrap-up' but does describe the gate run. Sharpen to something a grader can grep: the Narrative names the gate command run with --session SES-006, or the closing commit.

suggestions.expectation: transcript.md shows no push, no PR opened, no merge
suggestions.reason: The transcript is executor-authored, so absence of a push there is weak evidence. Require git-state.txt to carry `git log --oneline origin/main..main` (or `git rev-parse main origin/main`) so an unpushed commit is shown mechanically.

No expectation checks the closing commit itself: that a `docs(session):` commit exists at HEAD containing only the session file and the regenerated index (stage-by-name, not `git add -A`). This run did it correctly and it went unscored; a run that leaves the session file uncommitted but a clean-looking `git status` after a stash would pass everything else.

No expectation checks that the Outcome is grounded rather than invented — e.g. that it names no commit or file that is absent from `git log`. This run's Outcome was honest (and unusually good at separating 'verified' from 'not verified'), but a fabricated 'shipped X' would pass the current set.

eval_feedback.overall: The set discriminates well on the file-boundary rules (own session file only, SES-005 untouched, no OVERVIEW churn, no outward-facing actions) and all were verified against the fixture. The reply-length bound is the one failure and looks like a skill/eval mismatch rather than a lapse; the commit contents and Outcome grounding are the gaps worth adding.
